raw:
The user wants uninstaller strings in English. Rules: no chatty phrasing, no apologies, no exclamation marks in error states, no question marks as titles, no "we", no "your"/"your" unless needed to distinguish, avoid mainland Chinese terms (not relevant for English but avoid "data"? Actually 數據 = data; the rule says no 大陸用語 like 數據 — Taiwan uses 資料. In English this maps to "data" vs... hmm. The rule is for Chinese usage, but the note says English and Japanese follow same spirit: no chatty phrasing, no apologies, no questions as labels, no disclaimers, no mention of unseen, no exclamation marks.

s1: title of dialog asking whether to uninstall — should not be a question (rule: no questions as titles). So "Uninstall App" or "Uninstall"? A title like "Uninstall" works. Or "Confirm Uninstall". Since the dialog asks whether to uninstall, title could be "Uninstall". Keep short: "Uninstall".

s2: button that performs uninstall: "Uninstall". But s1 is also "Uninstall" — duplicate is fine, but maybe title "Uninstall App" and button "Uninstall". Better: s1: "Uninstall App" — hmm, title asking whether to uninstall. Titles like "Uninstall" are fine. Button "Uninstall", keep button "Cancel" (rule: cancel should be proper "Cancel" analog). s3: button that keeps the app — "Keep App" or "Cancel". The instruction says don't write "Cancel" as casual alternatives; "Cancel" itself is fine. s3 could be "Cancel" or "Keep". "Keep" is descriptive. I'll use "Cancel" — it keeps the app and closes dialog. But s3 says "the button that keeps the app" — "Keep" might be clearer. Either is fine. I'll use "Cancel".

Wait — rule: 不要重複標題已經說過的話 (don't repeat what the title already said). If title is "Uninstall" and button is "Uninstall", that's standard, but the rule suggests avoid repetition? That rule is more about body text repeating title. Buttons repeating titles is common. To be safe: title "Uninstall App"? Then button "Uninstall" isn't repetition of title exactly. Or title "Uninstall", button "Uninstall". Hmm, the rule 不要重複標題已經說過的話 — I'd interpret as body text. Button "Uninstall" under title "Uninstall" is somewhat redundant. Alternative: title "Uninstall App", button "Uninstall", keep "Cancel".

s4: status line while files are being removed: "Removing files..." — ellipsis is fine? Progressive states often use ellipsis. "Uninstalling..." is fine too. Avoid chatty. "Removing files…" — use "..." ASCII. I'll use "Removing files..." or "Uninstalling...". Since uninstall encompasses it, "Removing files..." is more specific. Keep no ending period per rule (rule says no period at end of labels and buttons; status line isn't a label... rule 不在標籤與按鈕結尾加句號 — status text maybe not). "Removing files..." with trailing ellipsis is standard.

s5: error when uninstall fails because app is still running, tell user what to do: "The app is still running. Close the app and try again." No apology, no exclamation. Avoid "your" — "Close the app" avoids possessive. Good.

Check rule about "我們" — avoid "we". Fine.

Output only JSON.```json
{"s1":"Uninstall App","s2":"Uninstall","s3":"Cancel","s4":"Removing files...","s5":"The app is still running. Close the app and try again."}
```

parsed.s5: The app is still running. Close the app and try again.
